scope: Design only; no verifier changes and no assertion that whole run67 passed strict verification.
proposed_rules: Default verifier behavior unchanged; explicit request ID opt-in returns recovered-journey scope, never whole-boot PASS.

Validate every raw prefix lifecycle record and its matching validated provenance/marker before selecting PID. Preserve priorPID269 main-only partial launch and every reject record as separate evidence. Reject malformed/duplicate/unpaired records rather than discard them.

Bind one exact host OPEN control to full serial send/completion, exact current boot and guest OPEN request/dispatched child/accepted callback/timing/normal child end. Exclude overlapping OPEN attempts before selected new process main and strict capture completion.

Select unique new-process five-hook timing sequence sameboot/timebase with main after named launcher request ticks; require accepted callback and original-libproc successful nonzero identity. Do not equate launcher PID358 with appPID360.

Require main1/appeared5/tap6 count0/0/1 for selected identity, complete event sequence provenance, fixed app identity and no selectedPID identity rejection. Preserve existing one-tap wire/ACK, capture hashes/QMP order, normal quit checks.

Without independent arrivals, accept only narrow case where prior processes have no appeared0 or tap1 marker. Then reviewed source gate could only use selectedPID appeared/tap. If prior appeared/tap exists, require genuinely retained chronological evidence; never manufacture a historical prefix.
Validate later records separately; later ordinary samePID events or OPENs must not be silently mistaken for initial strict records. Do not weaken existing default late-process checks.
limits: Observed clock ordering associates named OPEN with new process but TCP peer identity remains unauthenticated; original-libproc verifies claimed app identity only.
No independent per-marker host arrival times exist. Retained raw ordering plus unique source-gated appeared/tap is the available chronology scope.
Prior launch remains failed/incomplete evidence; successful recovery does not retroactively validate initial launch.
Manual visual0→1 review remains separate from raw record/capture verification.
